subject: Playbook sync: lab session checklist + payload handoff
messages:
From: Alex Rivera <alexr@acrodata.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.com>
Cc: POC Coordinator <poc@acrodata.com>
Date: 2026-11-01T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Initial: hands-on lab & payload handoff

Hi Dylan,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. The team (data + security) wants to move to a hands-on lab next week to validate routing and a couple of load scenarios. High level asks:
- 90-minute working session: prompt walk-through, routing options, and a short load/canary run.
- We will provide a ~200-row sample prompt CSV (anonymized) and a separate set of 40 evaluation prompts.
- Need guidance on redaction guidelines and expected timing for ingest.

Can you propose 2 possible time slots and confirm who from Redwood should join (routing + infra + sales)? Also let us know preferred format for the sample CSV and any header conventions.

Cheers,
Alex
Alex Rivera
Head of ML Ops, AcroData

---
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.com>
To: Alex Rivera <alexr@acrodata.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-02T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Initial: hands-on lab & payload handoff

Alex — thanks, happy to run this. Proposed options (PST):
- Tue 2026-11-10 10:00–11:30
- Thu 2026-11-12 13:00–14:30

Attendees from our side: me (solutions lead), Marissa (engineer — routing/load), Ben (CS — evals & success). Lauren can join for commercial/rollout items if needed.

Regarding sample format:
- CSV, UTF-8, header row with columns: id, prompt_text, expected_output (optional), metadata_tags.
- For routing tests include a column route_tag for 0/1 values we can map to model variants.
- Provide an additional small evaluation set (JSONL or CSV) with golden outputs if you have them.

On redaction: please follow the attached redaction_guidelines.pdf. Quick summary: remove PII, replace IDs with stable pseudonyms (e.g., user_###), redact free-form SSNs/credit cards. If you expect retention-sensitive fields, call them out in metadata so we can mask on ingress.

We can run a short canary load (1–2k tokens/sec) in the last 20 minutes to validate routing and KV cache behavior. Marissa — can you confirm the canary plan and any capacity considerations?

Thanks,
Dylan
Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference

Attachment stubs: redaction_guidelines.pdf (pdf)

---
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Rivera <alexr@acrodata.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-03T10:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Initial: hands-on lab & payload handoff

Quick operational notes:
- Canary plan: start with 5 concurrent sessions, ramp to ~25 over 12 minutes, hold for 8 minutes, then spike to 60 for 2 minutes (short spike verifies autoscaler/fallback).
- Routing test: include route_tag values for at least three categories (low-cost, high-quality, fallback). I recommend we map: 0 -> quantized small, 1 -> standard medium, 2 -> high-quality (no quant).
- KV/prefix caching: add some repeated prefixes in ~30% of prompts to see cache hit behavior.

For sample payloads: send separate CSVs: prompts.csv (200 rows), evals.csv (40 rows), and a small canary_input.csv (40 rows for ramp/spike). Identify any rows with longer sequences > 1024 tokens so we can pick buffer.

I will prepare the canary_load_plan.xlsx and share before the session. If you expect private VPC rules or IP allowlists, send them now so networking can be prepared.

Marissa
Principal Systems Engineer

Attachment stubs: canary_load_plan.xlsx (xlsx)
